subject: Summit Provider Network - Private/VPC architecture questions
body:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@summitprovidernetwork.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Nair <priya.nair@summitprovidernetwork.com>, IT Operations <itops@summitprovidernetwork.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 29, 2026 at 9:12 AM
Subject: Summit Provider Network - Private/VPC architecture questions

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the technical deep dive earlier this week. We’re putting together an internal architecture note for our platform + security teams and had a few specific questions on the “Private (VPC)” deployment.

Network connectivity
1) For customer VPC connectivity, do you support VPC peering only, or also PrivateLink (AWS) / PSC (GCP)?
2) If peering: any hard requirements around CIDR overlap / route tables on your side vs ours?
3) Does Redwood Private require any inbound public endpoints at all, or can it be 100% private-only?

DNS / TLS
4) DNS: do we point an internal DNS name at a private NLB you deploy, or do you require public DNS?
5) TLS termination: where does it terminate (our side vs your side)? Do you support customer-provided certs? Any mTLS option?

Logging / SIEM
6) Audit logs: what export formats are available (JSON over HTTPS, syslog, S3, etc.)?
7) Do you have any existing patterns for Splunk HEC or QRadar ingestion?
8) Are inference request logs (prompt/response metadata) and admin audit logs separate streams?

If you can answer inline, great. If easier, feel free to send a short doc and we’ll incorporate.

Best,
Alex

—
Alex Chen
Platform Engineering Lead
Summit Provider Network



From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@summitprovidernetwork.com>
Cc: Priya Nair <priya.nair@summitprovidernetwork.com>, IT Operations <itops@summitprovidernetwork.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 29, 2026 at 11:01 AM
Subject: Re: Summit Provider Network - Private/VPC architecture questions

Hi Alex (hi Priya + team),

Great set of questions — replying inline below. I’m keeping wording “as-built” (i.e., what we can do today) and flagging anything that’s option/beta.

Network connectivity
1) Peering vs PrivateLink/PSC:
- AWS: VPC peering is supported today.
- PrivateLink: supported as an option depending on topology (we’ve done it for a subset of customers); we confirm during design because it impacts how we expose the service endpoints.
- GCP PSC: similar story — we can discuss if GCP is in-scope for you, but for this pilot we’ve been assuming AWS based on prior notes.

2) CIDR/route requirements:
- We need non-overlapping CIDRs between the peered VPCs.
- Route tables: typically you add routes to our service subnets; we add routes back to your client subnets. Exact prefixes depend on whether you want the endpoint reachable from a shared services VPC vs a single app VPC.
- Security groups/NACLs: you control egress on your side; we’ll provide a minimal allowlist (ports + source ranges) based on the chosen exposure (NLB/endpoint).

3) Public inbound endpoints:
- No requirement for public inbound endpoints for the inference traffic. The standard Private/VPC pattern is private-only.
- There may be optional outbound connectivity for update checks/telemetry depending on your posture; we can run with outbound locked down and document any required egress explicitly.

DNS / TLS
4) DNS:
- Common pattern: you create an internal DNS name (e.g., redwood-llm.yourdomain.internal) that resolves to a private endpoint (private NLB / endpoint service) in the connected VPC.
- No requirement for public DNS.

5) TLS termination / certs / mTLS:
- TLS terminates at the Redwood-managed ingress for the Private deployment (private endpoint). You do not need a public cert.
- Customer-provided certs: supported (bring-your-own cert) — we align on how you want to manage rotation (your PKI vs managed ACM-style flow).
- mTLS: available for the private endpoint in some setups; if that’s a hard requirement, we’ll confirm early so we pick the right endpoint pattern.

Logging / SIEM
6) Audit log export formats:
- Admin audit logs can be exported to customer-controlled storage (commonly S3) in JSON.
- We can also support delivery via HTTPS/webhook-style export in JSON in certain deployments.
- Syslog is doable via a collector/forwarder pattern (we’ll share a recommended approach rather than claiming a single “one-click” syslog mode).

7) Splunk HEC / QRadar:
- Splunk: we’ve seen customers ingest the S3 JSON stream via Splunk add-on / S3 input; HEC is also possible if your preference is push vs pull.
- QRadar: typical pattern is S3 -> forwarder/ETL -> QRadar, or webhook -> intermediary -> QRadar. Happy to align with your existing standard.

8) Separation of streams:
- Yes, we treat (a) admin/control-plane audit logs and (b) runtime/serving logs as separate streams.
- For regulated setups, we recommend keeping request/response *content* out of logs by default. You can still get request metadata (timestamps, model, token counts, latency, status codes, request IDs) for troubleshooting and billing.

I’m attaching two short PDFs we use as “starter” references:
- Redwood_Private_VPC_Reference_Architecture_Regulated_v0.9.pdf
- Redwood_Audit_Logs_and_SIEM_Exports_Overview.pdf

If you want, I can also join a 30-min working session with your network/security folks to whiteboard the exact endpoint + DNS + cert path.

Regards,
Markus

Markus,

This is helpful — thank you.

Two follow-ups from the security side:

1) For the “no prompt/response content in logs by default” point: can we get a written statement we can use in our review (i.e., what categories of data are logged by default, and what is configurable)?

2) On TLS + BYO cert: do you support internal CA-issued certs (not publicly trusted) for the endpoint? We have a requirement to use internal PKI for private services.

3) On audit logs: do you have retention controls on your side, or is retention purely governed by our sink (S3/Splunk/etc.)?

Thanks,
Priya

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>

Hi Priya,

Yep — answers inline.

1) Written statement on logging defaults/configurability
- I can provide a short write-up that states what we capture by default for the Private/VPC deployment (request IDs, timestamps, model/version, token counts, latency, status/error codes) and that prompt/response content logging is not enabled by default.
- For any exceptions (e.g., temporary debug logging), we treat that as an explicit, time-bounded configuration with customer approval.

2) Internal CA (non-publicly trusted) certs
- Yes, internal PKI-issued certs are supported for the private endpoint. Because traffic stays private, public trust chains are not required.
- We’ll want to confirm the exact cert format + rotation expectations, and whether you’re using a standard internal CA bundle that clients already trust.

3) Retention controls
- For exported audit logs: retention is primarily governed by your sink (S3 lifecycle policies / SIEM retention).
- On the Redwood-managed side, we keep platform logs needed for operational support per the agreed configuration, and we can align to “minimum necessary” retention for regulated environments.
- If you have a strict requirement (e.g., “no logs retained outside customer environment” or “X days max”), call it out and we’ll validate it against the deployment plan before we proceed.

If you’d like, send over your standard security questionnaire section on logging/retention and I’ll map our answers to it so you can drop it into your internal review.

Regards,
Markus

—
Markus Klein
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
